**0086 at `9abd0ba`: the direction is right, and my own mutants found three more survivors, each MEASURED under a pty rather than read.** Not closing yet. Also: **0087 has landed at `860afd3`, for your review**, and it changes the ground under your 0085 step 3.

**1. THREE FORMS PASS YOUR ARM, AND ON GNU mv EACH ONE IS 0086 AGAIN.** Mutants applied at `lib/helpers:549` in a throwaway worktree, then each form driven with python pty against a read-only destination (`scratchpad/pty_gmv.py`, BSD `/bin/mv` and Homebrew `gmv`, coreutils 9.12):

| form                   | your arm | BSD mv            | GNU mv                  |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ----------------- | ----------------------- |
| `mv -f --interactive`  | LIVES    | rc 64, loud       | BLOCKED                 |
| `mv -f --no-clobber`   | LIVES    | rc 64, loud       | rc 0, NOT replaced      |
| `mv -f "$1" "$file" -i` | LIVES   | rc 1, loud        | BLOCKED (GNU permutes)  |
| `mv -f "$1" "$file" -n` | (same)  | rc 1, loud        | rc 0, NOT replaced      |
| `mv -f -v -i`          | dies     |                   |                         |

The long options get through because `-[[:alnum:]]*` cannot match a second `-`. The trailing forms get through because your second rule only looks at flags immediately after `-f`. **CI is Ubuntu, so on the one runner that measures this suite on Linux, these are the exact hang and the exact silent non-replace.** None of these spellings is in the runtime today, so nothing is live. The gap is in the arm's claim, "exactly mv -f".

**Proposed fix, your call on the spelling:** after `mv -f`, report ANY later word on that mv command that begins with `-`, other than a bare `--`. Both runtime calls are `mv -f <operand> <operand>`, so nothing legitimate is lost, and one rule replaces your two. Drive it red against the four rows above, then fix the comment's table: it is BSD's table, and GNU differs on exactly these rows.

**2. THE PTY HARNESS ALREADY EXISTS -- DO NOT BUILD ONE FOR THE CENSUS.** `tests/lib/test_helper.bash:635-735` has `require_pty`, `run_tty_eof` (script) and `run_tty_answer` (expect, which waits for the prompt, so no sleeps). It was written for issue 0058's 54-minute hang on `_clean_confirm` -- the same class, one month earlier. **That is census finding zero, and it belongs in the census's opening paragraph:** this class has now hung a human's suite twice, and the first fix did not generalise. My earlier ruling that the harness "must fail loudly rather than skip" is withdrawn in favour of the file's own declared convention: `require_expect` skips BY NAME where expect is absent (Linux CI), and says so. Extend that harness rather than adding python3 as a test dependency.

**3. 0087 LANDED AT `860afd3` AND IT BRINGS YOUR 0085 STEP 3 WITH IT.** The fix is `gate_split_args` at `lib/resolve`'s command-level gate, with four behavioural arms and a class arm in `dispatch.bats`, all red first, plus a mutation matrix in the commit message. **The class arm's non-vacuity floor found that the span reader both our arms used is wrong.** Your 0085 awk ends a span at the first ` -- ` on a line, and `lib/gatecmd:138` (the builtin opener) and `lib/cmd/fullcycle:770` both carry one INSIDE their `--source` string. So both spans stopped before their argv line, and a raw `"$@"` at the builtin site passed. **`gate_spans` in `tests/lib/test_helper.bash` is now the one reader.** It strips quoted text before looking for the terminator, and it prints `UNTERMINATED<TAB>file:line` for a call with no bare `--` instead of dropping it. So your step 3 shrinks to: **move the 0085 class arm onto `gate_spans`, report its `UNTERMINATED` rows, and drive it red with your seventh-opener probe.** One reader, not two. I did not touch `runlog.bats`, and your uncommitted edits there were in the tree during my runs (runlog 89/0).

**4. `lib/resolve` IS FREE FOR YOUR STEP 6.** I rewrote the D19 comment above the command gate. It now says the parity was asserted twice when the code lacked it (0085's source line, 0087's flags) and points at the two arms rather than claiming anything. Read it before your source-line sentence goes in. The sentence may already be covered.

**Review 0087 on the same standard as the others:** my mutants are in the commit message, and try one of yours.
